matched_rules.because: Multiple chillers (redundant cooling systems) failed simultaneously, and the standby switchover did not take effect, so the site cannot assume remaining cooling capacity is sufficient.
Mechanical cooling is down and temperatures are rising across multiple server rooms, so the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer and the buffer must be treated as finite.
Temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient, so progressive thermal load reduction should be used before full shutdown.

next_actions.action: Immediately assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature; if not, plan to power down servers to prevent an even longer outage or damage to machines.
Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted; expect automated device shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded.
Progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space, considering termination of non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs; if insufficient, power down servers.

escalate.reason: Simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems with rising temperatures and risk of exceeding safe operating thresholds.

not_covered: Chiller manufacturer involvement and manual isolation/restoration of individual chillers are not addressed by any rule in the pill.
